title: Prevention of Mental Health Disorders Using Internet- and Mobile-Based Interventions: A Narrative Review and Recommendations for Future Research
extended_summary:
This narrative review examines whether Internet- and mobile-based interventions (IMIs) can prevent the onset of mental health disorders, and what research gaps remain. The paper is motivated by the limited reach of traditional face-to-face prevention programs, especially given shortages of clinicians and barriers such as travel, time, and stigma. It asks whether scalable digital preventive interventions can reduce first onset or relapse of disorders, particularly in populations without a full mental disorder at baseline.

The paper synthesizes randomized trials of IMIs across several prevention types: indicated prevention for subthreshold depression and anxiety symptoms, selective prevention for eating disorders and depression risk factors, universal prevention in adolescents, and relapse prevention after prior depressive episodes. The interventions were mostly Internet-delivered cognitive behavioral or mindfulness-based programs, sometimes with guided self-help, asynchronous coach feedback, or occasional mobile reminders. The reviewed studies included adults, young adults, adolescents, and one school-based sample, with contexts such as workers, epilepsy patients, students, and previously hospitalized adults.

The review concludes that evidence is still limited, but there is the most consistent support for indicated prevention of depression. Evidence for anxiety prevention is not positive, and eating-disorder prevention appears promising only in very high-risk subgroups. The authors argue that the field needs larger and more rigorous trials, better diagnostic assessment at baseline and follow-up, stronger attention to human support formats, and more work on mobile features, prediction algorithms, and dissemination strategies. They also emphasize that many studies used small samples, self-report outcomes, or lacked long-term follow-up, limiting confidence in the findings.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative review and recommendations paper, not an empirical K-12 intervention study. It summarizes prior studies but does not itself report a primary causal design or original outcome data in education settings.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct educational intervention impact estimate to map to the K-12 framework. Its value here is conceptual only, helping define baselines and support models rather than demonstrating measured impact.
